card.architecture: Qwen-Image 20B MMDiT base (Qwen2.5-VL encoder) + InstantX 2B inpainting ControlNet, ImagePadForOutpaint canvas extension
card.summary: Extend an image past its edges with base Qwen-Image. The canvas is padded by pad_left/top/right/bottom (source-native pixels) and only the new border is generated; the InstantX ControlNet conditions that border on the known pixels so it continues the existing scene rather than inventing a fresh one, and the original area is composited back untouched.
card.pick_when: You want to widen the framing or add head/foot room and have Qwen-Image fill the new margin in keeping with the scene.

prompt.guidance: Describe the WHOLE enlarged picture in plain prose — the new border is generated to match it. The pad_* amounts (source pixels) come from the frame editor.
prompt.example: A wide shot of a bookstore storefront at dusk, wet pavement stretching into the street, neighbouring shopfronts on either side
prompt.instructions: Natural language, EN or ZH. Recommended: 20 steps, cfg ~2.5, euler/simple. Extend in moderate increments — a very large pad in one pass gives the ControlNet little context to continue from.

speed.measured_note: 20B INT8 ConvRot (native Ampere tensor cores) plus a 4.2 GB BF16 ControlNet on 24 GB; the ControlNet will be offloaded. Not yet benchmarked on this box.

ui_help.note: Drag the frame out on the sides you want to extend, describe the whole enlarged scene, and send. 'Mask edge blur' softens the join to the original.
ui_help.good_for: extending a photo's canvas on any side while keeping the original

edit_use_cases: outpaint: extend the canvas on any side and fill the new border in keeping with the existing scene
